sections.h2: Your options for a fast Shoreview sale
sections.html:
There are three ways to sell: through an agent, to a buyer you find yourself, or for cash with no repairs required. The best fit turns on the work the house needs and your deadline.

  • Hire an agent if the house is clean and updated and several weeks of showings are fine.
  • Sell directly if a buyer is already lined up and you are comfortable writing the purchase agreement and disclosures.
  • Go with cash if the house needs work, is a rental or part of an estate, or has to close on a firm date.

Shoreview, in Ramsey County, is a second-ring suburb just north of Saint Paul. It has seven lakes, led by Turtle Lake, Snail Lake, Lake Owasso and Island Lake, and Drivers rely on Interstate 35W, Interstate 694 and County Highway 96. Land area is 10.77 square miles.

The city counted 25,043 people in 2010 and 26,921 in 2020. The July 2025 estimate, 26,906, is nearly identical, so the market is mostly existing houses changing hands.

The city is split between Mounds View (District 621) and Roseville (District 623), and which one a buyer gets depends on the side of the line the house is on. A listing should name the district that applies.

Owners live in 80.2 percent of Shoreview homes, about four in five, and the typical owner's home is valued at $383,700. The average commute is 22.2 minutes.

How much cleanup a sale needs often comes down to permits. Closing out an open or missing one now beats scrambling after a buyer's inspection turns it up.

  • Permits: roofing, siding, window, door, electrical, mechanical and plumbing jobs need one. Contractors apply online, and homeowners email permits@shoreviewmn.gov or go to City Hall.
  • Plan review: when a permit needs it, expect up to 10 working days.
  • Smaller jobs: fences, driveways, patios and sheds of 200 square feet or less are handled by Community Development, 651-490-4680.
  • Safety items: handouts cover decks, egress windows, finished basements, smoke alarms and carbon monoxide alarms.

If the lot is by a lake or slopes, ask Community Development about the erosion and sediment control handout, because grading standards are being updated. Overnight street parking is banned from 2 to 5 a.m. A permit covers up to seven days and five vehicles, handy during a move-out, though dumpsters and storage pods can't go on the street.

sections.h2: Rental licenses and selling a rental
sections.html:
Each rental property needs a license, which the city grants only when the unit meets city regulations and municipal utility bills and real estate taxes are paid in full. More than 600 rental locations are on the city's list.

There are three license types: a general dwelling license for a single-family home with an inspection every other year, a short-term rental license for stays of 30 days or less with an annual inspection and extra parking rules, and a multiple dwelling license for four or more units. Licenses expire December 31 and renew each year. The city began licensing short-term rentals and inspected over 300 rental homes in 2025.

When you sell a rented house, the city has a form to void the license once the property is sold. Settle that, and any unpaid utility bill, at the closing table so the next owner starts clean.

Ramsey County sends two mailings each year. The first arrives in mid-March with the tax statement, showing both half-year amounts, and a notice of valuation and classification that sets next year's taxes. The second arrives in November, listing proposed taxes along with the levy and budget meeting dates.

Property Tax Services is at 90 Plato Boulevard West in Saint Paul, 651-266-2222. Deeds and mortgages are recorded with the Recorder and Registrar of Titles at 651-266-2050. Staff there can't help complete legal forms, and a recorded document is permanent, so have the deed reviewed before it goes in.

  • Ask Property Tax Services for the amount due on both halves of the current year.
  • Ask the Recorder which document types the sale needs, since fees and requirements differ by document.
  • For an estate sale, confirm who has authority to sign before scheduling the closing.
  • Read the November mailing: it previews next year's taxes and the budget meetings where residents can comment, which a buyer may ask about.

Start with the paper that can hold up a closing. Get the two half-year tax amounts from the county, check for open permits at City Hall, and, if the house is rented, line up the rental license and the form that voids it. Then decide how to sell. A listing adds showings, a buyer's mortgage and an appraisal. A cash sale skips those and leaves title work and the tenant's move-out date as the main timing issues.

For a rented house, settle the tenant's move-out date first, since a buyer who wants the house empty needs it in the contract. For an estate, confirm who can sign before any closing is scheduled. Either way, a seller with permits, taxes and licenses sorted tends to close sooner than one still chasing paper.

On closing day, the practical checklist is short. Bring photo ID for each owner who signs. Have the final utility readings and any unpaid city bill cleared so nothing follows the buyer. If the house was a rental, hand over the lease paperwork and let the city know the license is being voided. If the buyer is paying cash, the title company will usually run the same checks on taxes, liens and the owner of record, so the answers you gathered early are useful on either route, and they keep the closing date from slipping. Sellers who wait until the week of closing to call the county or the city usually find that one small item, such as a permit or a utility balance, needs several days to clear.

faqs.q: How fast can a Shoreview house sell for cash?
faqs.a: A cash sale can close in a few weeks when the title is clear, since there is no lender underwriting to wait on. A lien, an unpaid utility bill or an unsettled estate can lengthen that. If the house is rented, settle the tenant's move-out date first.

faqs.q: Does Shoreview require a rental license for a single-family house?
faqs.a: Yes. A single-family rental needs a general dwelling rental license, which includes an inspection every other year, and the license renews each December 31. The city issues it only when utility bills and real estate taxes are paid in full.

faqs.q: What happens to a Shoreview rental license when I sell?
faqs.a: Use the city's form to void the license once the property has sold. Doing it promptly stops renewal notices and shows the city the unit changed hands.

faqs.q: When does Ramsey County mail property tax notices?
faqs.a: The tax statement and value notice go out in mid-March, and the proposed tax notice arrives in November. The statement shows the first and second half amounts for the year.

faqs.q: Is a permit needed to fix up a Shoreview house before listing?
faqs.a: Often yes. Roofing, siding, windows, doors, electrical, mechanical and plumbing work all need permits, and fences, driveways and small sheds go through Community Development. Call building inspections at 651-490-4683 to confirm before starting.
